fixes.explanation: Yes, baker. Paul says, “…there must be differences among you to show which of you are approved.” (1 Corinthians 11:19) Just before that, he says he hears there are divisions among them when they come together as a church (verse 18). So this verse comes right on the heels of those divisions in their gatherings. The differences are there to show who is approved.

Yes. Jesus says, “This cup is the new covenant in My blood…” (1 Corinthians 11:25) Paul is passing on what he received from the Lord about the night Jesus was betrayed. That night Jesus took bread first, and then in the same way, after supper, He took the cup. The cup is the second half of what Jesus gave them to do in remembrance of Him.

Paul doesn't use that word here. He says they “…proclaim the Lord’s death until He comes.” (1 Corinthians 11:26) Jesus called the bread His body, which is for them, and the cup the new covenant in His blood. Both point to His death, so that's what they proclaim.

Paul doesn't say honor. He says anyone who eats and drinks without recognizing the body “…eats and drinks judgment on himself.” (1 Corinthians 11:29) Just before this, he says each one must examine himself before he eats of the bread and drinks of the cup (verse 28). So the person is meant to stop and look at himself first, not just dig in. Skip that, and Paul says the result is judgment, not honor.
